summary: First test of the breakdown scenario. Backend: 30/30 unit tests in test_breakdown.py pass, and 14/14 live API tests pass (new file tests/test_iter18_breakdown_live.py). Covered: tire question -> researching -> providers (6 providers, phone/rating/distance/facts, call_card, total about 6 s, well under 20 s), quotes contain the amounts, tow goes straight to research, unknown id returns 404, the follow-ups call cheapest (dial_phone set) / how far / Comchek / truck stop (not hijacked, route_set), and normal intents (Reno, hotel, mute). An extra live probe with the mechanic flow passed for route me to the mobile one (route_set), anyone else, read reviews, Comchek and call the closest. Frontend at 390x844: everything requested works. Skip onboarding, type to the copilot, question caption, 'Checking who's around…', providers-list with 6 cards, all filter and sort chips, tell-them card expanding, provider details expanding, sort order changes, filters reduce the list, Call opens tel:9165896775, Share opens sms:?body=..., Route shows the route card, end-route returns to the providers list, and close returns to 'Where to next?'. No console errors. 5 live research runs used (tire, tow, 2 UI, mechanic); the other UI runs used mocked /api/agent and /api/breakdown responses. Problems found: (1) the answer to the tire question changes the kind from tire to trailer; (2) the pending clarifying question can't be escaped, so any next utterance starts a paid research run; (3) the first tap on Route for a provider takes 6-12 s because /api/route waits for the satellite parking check; (4) review-backed wording is used for ETAs that came from a website; plus some minor issues. No deprecated Expo packages detected.

critical.issue: breakdown._handle re-parses the pending text plus the answer, and the LLM's kind overrides pending['kind']. Answering 'trailer, can't roll, come out to me' to the tire question gave kind=trailer (backend log: 'breakdown research kind=trailer mode=mobile_needed' for both UI runs), so it searches trailer-repair instead of tire service, the call card loses the Tire row, and problem becomes 'trailer can't roll, come out to me' (the blown tire is lost). Fix: keep pending['kind'] always (services/breakdown.py:414-416) and merge the pending detail.

No escape from breakdown_pending. Whatever the driver says next ('never mind, take me to Reno', 'mute directions') goes to start_research, and PARSE's 'breakdown': false is ignored (services/breakdown.py:410-417). Each research run costs about $0.13 and hijacks the turn. Fix: if d.get('breakdown') is False, pop pending and return None so the normal agent handles it. (Found by code review; not run live, to save cost.)

minor.issue: wait_time has no source field. known() says 'drivers say they come out ...' and the UI says '... min by reviews' even when the quote is from the website ('30-60 min ETA guaranteed in Sacramento County.' for 99 Glide). The spoken answer said 'drivers say they show up in thirty to sixty minutes', which misattributes a website claim to drivers.

The range isn't checked against the numbers in the quote. A+ Truck Repair had quote 'Response time is usually 30 min.' but typical_min 30-45. Prices are checked this way; wait_time isn't (providers_search.py:366-372).

'check engine light came on and I'm losing power' was classified mode=shop_ok and no 'Can it still drive?' question was asked, even though the driver never said it still drives. The classifier infers mode against the 'only what the driver said' rule.

minor.endpoint: follow-up 'how far is the second one'
minor.issue: The reply was 'The second one is four point two miles away. They don't mention that, ask when you call.' The NOT_IN_FACTS sentence is tacked onto a correct answer and contradicts it.
The on-screen summary spells numbers out ('open twenty-four seven', 'thirty to sixty minutes') because SUMMARY_SYSTEM's spoken rule leaks into the summary. Use digits for the summary.

For 30 min after providers, every utterance costs an extra LLM call (about 1 s) before the normal intent runs. 'anyone else' always offers a tow, even in tow/shop_ok contexts, and never widens the search.

ui_bugs.issue: The first tap on Route for a provider showed 'Setting route…' for over 5 s in the live UI run. The RCA is under rca_of_issue. Cached places route in 1 s (verified). The parking card then shows 'Unlikely to fit a truck' for a truck-repair shop the driver may not be able to roll to, which is misleading in mobile_needed mode.
'out within 30–60 min by reviews' even when the source is the website (see the backend wait_time issue).

issues: The filter and sort chips are 36px tall with no hitSlop, under the 44px minimum touch target.

The long 4-5 line summary plus the 'What to tell them' card push the provider cards below the fold. Only the top of the first card is visible without scrolling, and nothing is visible once the tell-them card is expanded. Consider a 2-line summary or putting the cards first.
The speech bubble with the spoken comparison covers the upper map and the provider pins while speaking.

action_items: breakdown._handle: when a pending question exists, keep pending['kind'] (don't let the re-parse turn tire into trailer) and keep the original detail ('blew a tire').
breakdown._handle: if the PARSE result has breakdown=false (the driver changed the subject), clear breakdown_pending and return None so the normal agent handles it.
Make provider Route fast: don't block /api/route on check_parking for breakdown providers. Skip it, or run it in the background via /api/parking.
Add a source to wait_time (review/website) and use it in known() and the UI ETA line instead of always saying 'drivers say' / 'by reviews'. Also check the wait range numbers against the quote.
The mechanic classifier should leave mode unknown unless the driver says whether the truck can move, so the 'Can it still drive' question gets asked.
Follow-up 'answer' replies: don't append NOT_IN_FACTS when the fact was answered. Use digits in the screen summary.
Design: chip touch targets of 44px or more (hitSlop), and a shorter summary or cards first so at least one full provider card is visible.
critical_code_review_comments: breakdown.py:414-416: the pending answer overrides the kind, and the 'breakdown' flag from PARSE is ignored.
server.py /api/route: asyncio.gather(route, check_parking) means the route response waits for the satellite vision check (6-12 s cold).
breakdown.py: _JOBS/_tasks and sessions live in process memory, so they don't survive a restart or multiple workers. Fine for the demo; document it.
breakdown.result(): after a 30 s timeout it returns 'search took too long' while the task keeps running and later fills sess['providers']. Follow-ups will then act on providers the UI never showed.
ProvidersList ETA line: when typical_min_low == typical_min_high (>0) it renders '30–30 min'.

success_rate.backend: 100% of the 14 live tests + 30 unit tests pass; 2 HIGH logic bugs found by log and code review
success_rate.frontend: about 95% (every requested flow works; provider route is slow on first tap)

seed_data_creation: None. /tmp/iter18_breakdown.json holds a real providers response and was used to mock /api/agent and /api/breakdown in the UI runs.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Live research costs about $0.13 per run. To test the UI cheaply, intercept /api/agent (return status=researching, research_id) and /api/breakdown/** with page.route using /tmp/iter18_breakdown.json. Grant geolocation 38.5816,-121.4944. Onboarding: onboarding-skip-button. Typing: type-button -> copilot-text-input -> copilot-send-button. On web, tel: goes through window.location (shows up as an aborted request to tel:...) and sms: goes through window.open.
rca_of_issue: Slow provider Route: index.tsx onPlacePress -> api.route -> server.py build_route awaits asyncio.gather(route, check_parking(place)). For a provider that hasn't been checked yet, check_parking runs the satellite plus vision check. Measured with curl: Norcal 11.6 s, SAA 6.2 s; 99 Glide took 0.2 s once cached. Reproduced by tapping Route on a fresh provider. Tire->trailer: the backend log shows 'breakdown research kind=trailer' after the answer 'trailer, can't roll, come out to me' to the tire question.
